title: Feldmann et al. (2021), Parallel convolutional processing using an integrated photonic tensor core, Nature 589, 52-58.
supports: Phase-change memory arrays and optical wavelength multiplexing perform specified convolution operations. This supports the combination of optical processing and retained weights.
boundary: The experiment is not evidence of A18's arbitrary coherent complex interface, verification protocol or total-system advantage. No projected speed from this paper is used as an A18 measurement.

title: Clements et al. (2016), Optimal design for universal multiport interferometers, Optica 3, 1460-1465.
supports: A constructive mesh decomposition supplies a design basis for unitary optical transformations.
boundary: Nonunitary targets need additional attenuation, embedding or other machinery. An ideal factorization does not prove a fabricated network can reach a requested error tolerance.

title: Chen et al. (2023), Non-volatile electrically programmable integrated photonics with a 5-bit operation, Nature Communications 14, 3465.
supports: Sb2S3 photonic devices demonstrate electrically retained multilevel settings and phase-error trimming.
boundary: Write latency, thermal separation and endurance depend on the actual device and pulse protocol. One headline switching time cannot specify an entire A18 rewrite and verification cycle.

title: Catala-Lahoz et al. (2026), High-speed non-volatile barium titanate field-programmable photonic gate array, Nature Photonics.
supports: The integrated ferroelectric architecture demonstrates retained individual cells. Its complex mesh configurations, including routing, filtering and unitary transformations, were characterized using volatile actuation.
boundary: Automated retained-state addressing of the full mesh remained future work. Fast volatile Pockels switching is not a retained rewrite latency; retained intermediate states use pulse protocols. This source does not establish the complete A18 instrument.

title: Du et al. (2017), Reservoir computing using dynamic memristors for temporal information processing, Nature Communications 8, 2204.
supports: Short-term dynamics in electronic WOx memristors supply temporal features used by a trained readout.
boundary: This is electronic device evidence. Its coupling to a photonic processor and the proposed A18 material-history law remain separate research tasks.

title: Perez-Lopez et al. (2020), Multipurpose self-configuration of programmable photonic circuits, Nature Communications 11, 6359.
supports: Experiments and optimization studies support calibrated control curves, automated configuration and routing in programmable photonic circuits.
boundary: No algorithmic convergence guarantee follows for every requested matrix, damaged circuit or larger mesh. An accepted A18 configuration still requires its own measured residual and holdout evidence.

title: Xie et al. (2025), Complex-valued matrix-vector multiplication using a scalable coherent photonic processor.
supports: A coherent processor uses an optical hybrid and balanced detection to recover both quadratures for complex-valued processing.
boundary: Its apparatus and calibration do not automatically qualify a different retained-state mesh. A18 must bind its own receiver gains, phase convention, uncertainty and operating range.
